order.why: Rule 1 3-of-3: two back-to-back stopping protons whose profiles rise monotonically from ~20k at 1007 to 250k at 1008 and 315k at 1000, plus the long track leaving at 26k; the far end 1009 shows a pi+ Bragg feeding a 14.5 cm decay muon, so the low-z end is the far end and rule 2 must not overturn this.

Rule 1: 31021 is a V apex with 2 of 2 prongs rising away (20 cm proton to a 151k stop at 31019, 7 cm heavy stub to a 152k stop at 31020), and the 41 cm MIP muon of cluster 8 extrapolates backwards from its 8000 end to within ~1 cm of 31021.

The lone 35 cm track rises monotonically along the proton template from 43000 at 17000 to 170000 at 17001, so it stops at 17001 and must start at 17000 (rule 1); the zoom shows nothing else within 10 cm of that cool free end.

Three-prong star with 3/3 rising away and every far end showing a genuine template-following Bragg - muon to 175k at 9001, proton to 300k at 9005, pion to 185k at 9004 - and the zoom shows three arrows radiating from 9003 with both hot branches heating up away from it.
Rule 1: 2 of 2 rise away, a 236 cm MIP track leaving and a 10.3 cm proton reaching 200548, with three further hadronic fragments (including a 5.8 cm proton rising to 116926) within 6 cm of the point.

Rule 1 with all three prongs starting near 32k at 8008 and rising away, the 8008-8007-8004 chain being one continuously rising 24 cm proton, and the 183 cm muon's backward line from 4001 passing within 1.6 cm of 8008 across the 21.6 cm gap.

Rule 1 at full strength: 17004 is a 119 degree V apex in all three projections with 2 of 2 prongs rising away, one a 292 cm flat-MIP muon running downstream to z=500 and the other a 26.6 cm prong that Bragg-stops at 17011 with a 189k stub.

Rule 8: 16 candidates in 13 clusters, all sub-cm blips except two isolated short high-dQ/dx stubs, spread over 100 cm of z with no convergence and no readable direction, so I abstain rather than invent a reason.

Rules 1 and 3: the 24 cm muon rises to 101k and stops at 11000 with a Michel-like blob 4.3 cm off that end, so the vertex is the cool upstream tip 11001. The competing 11002 is a 146-degree degree-2 junction (trap 3) where both segments read ~1 MIP with no junction charge, so I read its 34-degree non-MCS kink as a hard scatter of one particle rather than a vertex.

Rule 1: the 183 cm muon has a sharp Bragg to 215k at 13000 and sits at MIP into 13001, and the 10.7 cm second prong ends dark red at 175k at 13003; the zoom shows a clean ~95 deg V in Z-Y at the most upstream candidate (z=221).

The 291 cm cluster is a straight flat-MIP through-going track whose 9003 split is exactly collinear (trap 3), leaving only a fragmented 11 cm chain (38+101+39) 25 cm off it, all dQ/dx flat, so I take its upstream end on rule 2 alone.

Collinearity trap in its purest form: the two prongs at 22010 meet at 180.0 deg and the tight zoom shows only a ~1.4 cm fit step with no third prong or stub, so although both ends Bragg away from it the event is a single straight 246 cm track and I am close to guessing.
Rule 1: the 89cm muon rises from MIP to a 210k Bragg at 12001, so it starts at 12000, where there is a vertex charge blob and a 7.6cm stub; the hot 5cm at 12000 is that blob, not a second Bragg.

Clusters 13 and 39 are one straight 330cm flat-MIP track (the join is 2cm and 173 deg, a reconstruction split), with no Bragg anywhere; one end lies on the y=+200 wall, so I took the interior, lowest-z end 39020, which has three or four sub-cm blips within 25cm as the hadronic recoil.
The 147 cm track has a monotone Bragg to 280k at 7001, so it starts at the cool interior end 7002, which also carries a short e stub and nearby blobs.

Rule 1 in its strong form: both prongs rise away, the 14.2 cm proton climbing monotonically to 190680 at 7001 and the 213 cm muon Bragging to 122852 at 7000, and the two prongs leave 7011 about 109 degrees apart so this is not the collinear degree-2 trap.
Rule 1: p4 shows a textbook monotone stopping-muon rise to 250000 e/cm over the last 3 cm at the 6002 end, so the flat-MIP 6000 end is where the track began.

11002 is a 172 degree collinear split (trap 3), while cluster 41's 6.4 cm MIP track is aligned to 11 degrees with the 11001-to-41007 gap vector and leaves 11001 at 89 degrees to the proton that Bragg-stops at 11000, making 11001 the real two-prong junction.

Rule 1 applied to the only real cluster: the 123 cm muon is flat MIP from 17000 and rises to a 420k Bragg at 17001, so 17000 is its start; but 17000 sits in the z=501/y=-194 corner and the track runs backward in z, so I am close to guessing between this and the handful of unreadable blobs at z=130-156.
Rule 1: both prongs Bragg at their far ends (160k and 220k) so it is a genuine junction, but they leave ~170 degrees apart so I drop a tier.

Neither end Braggs (the 19000 end is one 175k point dropping to MIP in 2 cm), so no stopping end exists; 19000 is the only interior endpoint, its blob reading as vertex charge, while 19001 sits in the y wall.

Rule 1: zoom shows the 128 cm muon leaving 7008 cool (MIP all the way to the z=498 downstream face, no Bragg) while the 39 cm proton rises monotonically away from 7008 to a 280k Bragg at 7005; the 5 cm mean at the muon end is only junction charge.

Both prongs leave 10002 at MIP and end in template-matching Bragg peaks (300k at 10000, 205k at 10001), which one particle cannot do, but the 176 degree back-to-back geometry is the collinearity trap so I drop a tier.

Diffuse multi-fragment EM event; 12001 sits at 2.5x MIP so it is a photon conversion and not the vertex, and the shower axis back-extrapolates upstream past this lobe onto a sub-cm cluster that p6 does not name, so this is the closest nameable proxy.

Rule 1: the 10 cm pi+ has a clean Bragg rise to 118k at 7005, so the vertex is the cool end of the chain; 7002 is the degree-2 kink (118 degrees) with locally elevated charge, 2.6 cm inside the free tip 7000.

Two independent stopping protons 65 cm apart (Bragg at 13000 and at 39026), so rule 1 is satisfied at both origins 13001 and 39025; I took 13001 because its proton carries ~6x the charge and its neighbourhood holds several more fragments, but rule 2 points the other way and this is close to a coin flip.

p4 shows the 16.5 cm segment rising over its last 4 cm to 175k at 2001 along the stopping template, so 2001 is the stopping end; rule 1 leaves 2000 as the start, and the two satellite dots lie further +z as rule 2 would expect.

Textbook 3-prong star: the zoom shows cool cyan points right at 6003 with a 27 cm hadron Bragging to 235k at 6000, a 12.4 cm pi+ Bragging to 205k at 6001, and an 18 cm e prong, i.e. everything comes out of 6003.

Whole event is one curved 16 cm MIP fragment in the detector corner; the second half averages ~75k against ~48k for the first, so it cools toward this end, but the trend rests on one 218k point plus weak means and rule 2 points the other way.

Fragmented shower event where every segment is flat MIP and no dQ/dx asymmetry exists; I take 92087 by rule 6 as the highest-degree (deg 3) junction and the point the arms toward cluster 17, cluster 89 and the cluster-91 knot all radiate from, but this is close to a guess.
